Run order planning

Give one item more demand than its stock covers, run planning on it, and read the orders LN suggests.

Status
Verified
Module
Enterprise Planning, Sales

Length

Updated

Before you start

  • You need a finished item with a BOM, its components, and a customer set up as a sold-to business partner. Create test items makes the items.

Procedure

1Check each item has a plan

Result
The finished item and each of its components opens in Item Order Plan.
Session
Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000)

Why LN works this way. Planning only works on an item that has a plan. An item without one isn't refused, it just isn't there, and nothing tells you why. A component needs a plan of its own too, or planning skips it without a word.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Open Item Order PlanA plan opens, often another item's, with Scenario and Plan Item at the top
1.2Click FindItem Order Plan - Find opens
1.3Plan Item has three boxes. Leave the first two as they are. Type the finished item in the third and press TabExamplePlan Item BAM-CHOP-PAIR, then BAM-ROD and BAM-SLEEVE
1.4Click OKThe finished item's plan opens, with Inventory on Hand under GeneralWrite downfinished itemon-hand
1.5Do steps 1.2 to 1.4 for each component in the item's BOMEach component's plan opensWrite downcomponents
Check each item has a plan: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
A row you expect isn't in the gridThe grid can open scrolled to its last rows. Scroll up
The item's plan doesn't openThe item has no plan. Add a row for your planning cluster on the Clusters tab of Item (tcibd0501m100), save, and look again

2Create a sales order to plan for

Result
A sales order for more of the finished item than you have is saved, at Free.
Session
Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench (tdsls4601m200)

Why LN works this way. Planning only acts on demand that stock doesn't cover. A sales order for more than you have on hand makes a shortfall, and planning should suggest orders for it. The order doesn't need approving for planning to see it.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Open Sales Order Intake WorkbenchThe list of sales orders
2.2At the top, click NewSales Order opens, empty
2.3Enter your customer in Sold-to Business Partner and press TabAddress fills in
2.4Set Planned Delivery Date to a week from todayExamplePlanned Delivery Date 7 days after the order dateWrite downdelivery date
2.5Click SaveStatus = FreeWrite downsales order number
2.6In the lines, click NewA new line
2.7Type the finished item from step 1.4 in Item and press TabExampleItem BAM-CHOP-PAIRThe item's description fills in
2.8Enter an Ordered Quantity larger than the on-hand from step 1.4ExampleOrdered Quantity 30Write downordered quantity
2.9Click Save
Create a sales order to plan for: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
LN refuses the item: item sales by sales office not presentThe item has no row for the order's sales office. Add one on the Sales Offices tab of Item (tcibd0501m100), then close the order and open it again
A change to the item has no effectThe order was already open when the item changed. Close it and open it again

3Put the order inside the horizon

Result
The finished item's Order Horizon date is after your sales order's delivery date.
Session
Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000)

Why LN works this way. The run makes planned orders only inside the order horizon. Your sales order can show in the plan after it, and still get nothing. You set the horizon as a number of days, and LN works out the date by counting working days on the calendar of the item's warehouse, so trust the date it shows.

StepActionYou should see
3.1In Item Order Plan, open the finished item's plan, as in steps 1.2 to 1.4Order Horizon under Horizons, and your sales order as a row in the grid
3.2Compare the horizon date with the delivery date from step 2.4. If the horizon is later, this task is done
3.3At the top, click References➔Item Details➔Items - PlanningItems - Planning opens for the same item
3.4Click the Horizons tabOrder Horizon as a number of days, with its date beside it
3.5Type a larger number of days in Order Horizon and press TabExampleOrder Horizon 30 daysThe date beside it moves
3.6Check the new date is after the delivery date from step 2.4Write downorder horizon
3.7Click OKItems - Planning closes, and Order Horizon in the plan shows the new date
Put the order inside the horizon: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Planning makes nothing for your sales orderThe delivery date is after the Order Horizon date. Raise the days again from step 3.3, and read the date LN shows rather than counting

4Run planning

Result
LN has planned the finished item and its components, and kept the links between each order and the demand it serves.
Session
Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000)

Why LN works this way. The run reads every demand inside the horizon, takes off what stock and existing orders already cover, and suggests planned orders for the rest. With child items included, it goes down through the BOM to the components. It also keeps which demand each planned order is for, which is what the pegging tree shows.

StepActionYou should see
4.1In the finished item's Item Order Plan, click GENERATE ORDERS... at the topGenerate Order Planning (Item) opens, with Scenario and Plan Item filled in for your item
4.2Check Include Child Items is selected
4.3Check Update Pegging Relations is selected
4.4Click GENERATELN asks Scenario must be rolled. Continue without rolling scenario?
4.5Click YESSelect Device opens, for the exception report
4.6Click CONTINUELN says Processing was successful. No report printed.
4.7Click OKThe dialog closes, and the plan shows new Planned Production Order rows
Run planning: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The finished item is planned but a component isn'tThe component has no plan, or its order horizon ends too early. Step 1.5
Nothing is planned for the finished itemCheck which item the run was started on. A run from a component doesn't plan the item above it. Run it again from the finished item
A component has a plan and still gets no planned orderThat can be right: planning suggests supply only for what stock doesn't cover. Read the component's Inventory on Hand before you change anything

5Read the planned orders

Result
The finished item's plan has planned production orders at Planned, and each component's plan has them as demand, met by planned purchase orders or stock.
Session
Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000)

Why LN works this way. One planned order plays two parts. On the finished item's plan it is supply. On each component's plan it is demand, and the component's plan has already answered it. A planned quantity can differ from the shortfall if the item's ordering data rounds it, to a minimum or a multiple.

StepActionYou should see
5.1In the finished item's Item Order Plan, click RefreshPlanned Production Order rows at Planned, each with its quantity under SupplyWrite downplanned production orders
5.2Open each component's plan, as in steps 1.2 to 1.4Each planned production order from step 5.1 is a row, with what it needs under Demand, and a Planned Purchase Order row or stock covers it
Read the planned orders: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
A planned quantity isn't the shortfallOrder-quantity rules in Items - Ordering (tcibd2100m000) round it
A component has no planned purchase order you expectedIf it is a purchase schedule item, supply goes straight to Purchase Control. Otherwise its stock may cover the need

6Read the pegging tree

Result
Under your sales order, the stock and planned orders add up to its quantity, at every level of the BOM.
Session
Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000)

Why LN works this way. The pegging tree follows the links the run kept. Upstream answers what will supply this demand; downstream answers what demand this order is for. There is a tree only if the run kept the links.

StepActionYou should see
6.1In the finished item's Item Order Plan, tick the row for the sales order from step 2.5
6.2At the top, click References➔Pegging Browser➔Pegging - UpstreamOrder Pegging opens in a new tab, with your sales order at the top
6.3Read the rows under the sales orderPlanned production orders, stock or both, adding up to the order's quantity
6.4Read the rows under each planned production orderA row for each component, and under it planned purchase orders, stock or both, adding up to that row's quantity
Read the pegging tree: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The tree is emptyThe run didn't keep the links, or the demand is after the Pegging Horizon (cprpd0100m000). Check step 4.3

Variations

Variations
CaseWhat changes
Planning every itemGenerate Order Planning (cprrp1210m000), Planning➔Order Planning➔Generate Order Planning, plans ranges of items instead of one, as a planner does every day. Its options are not assumed to match Generate Order Planning (Item)
Net changeSelect Run a Net Change Planning before step 4.4, and LN plans only from the first net-change date
Master planningWith Master Plan selected on Items - Planning (cprpd1100m000), the item also has a master plan, beyond the order horizon. That is its own guide, not written yet
